discrepancies: W1 gate uses frozen constant: 'm6_entrypoints = 8 if has_m6_indexing else 0' (run_m7_3_write_authority_gate.py:59). The '8' is asserted, not dynamically counted from 8 distinct entrypoints. Underlying claim (M6 indexing wired into production indexer) is genuinely TRUE per runner.py:1100-1134 inspection.

W4 gate is hardcoded: 'r4 = True  # Will be verified by code inspection' (run_m7_3_write_authority_gate.py:80). The gate itself does not test the no-silent-fallback clause; it delegates to the Fresh Verifier. I verified by code inspection: runner.py:1128-1134 raises IndexIntegrityError on M6 indexing failure (no silent swallow). Direct test with bogus legacy DB path raised OperationalError rather than returning stats.

W3 materialization evidence is misleading: the gate checks .dsh-control/m6_research/corpus/FreeRTOS-Kernel/.fw-context/index-m6.db (size=4481024, 5736 facts), but that corpus DB contains fact kinds (Body=154, ConditionalState=1009, FileContent=6, EnumConstant=13, Field=89) that index_legacy_db_into_m6 does NOT produce. The corpus was populated by the research harness, NOT the production path. However, independent materialization IS proven: running index_legacy_db_into_m6 against tests/fixtures/legacy_rows2/index.db produced 2 enriched Function facts with payload fields (file, line, qualified_name, signature, docstring, end_line, is_definition, is_virtual, is_pure_virtual, is_template, parent_usr, template_usr), plus registered World (m6_world_builds: 1 row, world_id=1, build_name='verifier-test') and BuildSet (m6_buildsets: 1 row, build_names_json=['verifier-test']).

m6_world_fact_refs table is 0 rows in both the independent test run and the corpus DB. Per m6_store.py:50 this table is 'legacy, deprecated by m6_world_builds'. The production path registers World via m6_world_builds (1 row in test run), so this is expected, not a gap. Corpus DB has m6_world_builds=0 because it was populated by a different (research) path that does not call register_world.

normal_path_dependencies_state.json still records normal_old_v2_finalization_dependencies=1 and normal_old_v2_fallbacks=3 (M7.5 targets). These are NOT M7.3 blockers: required_writes=0 is the M7.3 gate criterion and it is satisfied. v2 finalize_world still runs but is no longer the sole required write authority.
summary: M7.3 WRITE_AUTHORITY migration is GENUINE, not fabricated. (1) index_legacy_db_into_m6 in src/fw_context_mcp/store_v2/m6_production_indexing.py is a REAL implementation that opens the legacy SQLite DB, reads symbols/call_sites/refs/overrides tables, and writes canonical M6 facts with enriched payloads (file, line, qualified_name, signature, docstring, end_line, is_definition, is_virtual, is_pure_virtual, is_template, parent_usr, template_usr) — it is NOT a v2 data copy (§8 anti-false-migration satisfied: fact_canon is canonical, e.g. Function(usr,signature,,none)). (2) It is wired into the MAIN production indexer runner.py run() function at lines 1100-1134, AFTER legacy indexing completes and BEFORE return config_hash — not a standalone script. (3) It is gated by FW_CONTEXT_M6_WRITE_AUTHORITY env var (default '1', truthy values: 1/true/yes/on). (4) On failure it raises IndexIntegrityError (not silent) — verified both by code inspection and by direct failure-path test. (5) Materialization proven independently: running the function against tests/fixtures/legacy_rows2/index.db produced 2 enriched Function facts in m6_shared_facts with payload_json containing all enriched fields, plus registered World (m6_world_builds) and BuildSet (m6_buildsets). (6) v2 required writes = 0 per normal_path_dependencies_state.json. The gate result (8/10 PASS, W7+W8 pending) accurately reflects state. Discrepancies found are gate-design weaknesses (frozen constants, hardcoded True, misleading W3 corpus pointer) — they do not invalidate the migration. Recommend Guardian G6 note the W3 corpus DB should be regenerated via the production path so W3 evidence matches the production indexer, not the research harness.
